hints: Which walk tells you the root right away? Once you know the root, how does the other walk tell you which values go left and which go right?

Use divide and conquer on index ranges of inorder. Take the next preorder value as the root. Its position in inorder (found with a value→index HashMap) splits the range into the left and right subtrees.

1. Map each inorder value to its index.
  2. Keep a pointer into preorder, starting at 0.
  3. build(lo, hi): if lo > hi, return null.
  4. Take preorder[ptr++] as the root and find its index m in inorder.
  5. Build the left child from (lo, m−1), then the right child from (m+1, hi).

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Do the same recursion, but find the root in inorder with a linear scan and copy subarrays at every step.

approaches.name: Optimal (index map + pointer)
approaches.idea: Look up the split point in O(1) with a HashMap and use one moving preorder pointer, building the left subtree first.

explain: Preorder [4,2,1,3,7] says the root is 4. In inorder [1,2,3,4,7], 4 sits at index 3, so [1,2,3] is the left subtree and [7] is the right subtree. The next preorder value, 2, is the root of the left part, with 1 on its left and 3 on its right. Then 7 becomes the right child of 4. The left subtree must be built before the right, because preorder lists all of the left subtree first. Distinct values make the map lookup unambiguous.
recognize: When you are given two traversal orders and asked to rebuild the tree, the root comes from preorder or postorder and the left/right split comes from inorder.
